context.stage: EPIC-2 Run 1: Entity Definition Format + Entity Command API

task.description:
Validate the design artefact for EXP-201 and EXP-202 (src/design/entities.md).

This is a HARD GATE — BACKEND-DEV cannot start until this returns PASS.

Run per-artefact checks:
1. python tools/lint_design_artefact.py src/design/entities.md

Then verify:
1. Every acceptance criterion in EXP-201 and EXP-202 has a corresponding design element
2. No implementation code is present (no Zig, SQL, or TypeScript code blocks)
3. All public function signatures are listed
4. Error taxonomy exists
5. Dependencies are documented
6. Classification per templates/lego-catalog.md is correct

EXP-201 acceptance criteria:
- An entity definition canonicalises + hashes deterministically
- Logical-shape versions are retained while referenced
- Validator rejects a field marked both queried and JSONB-only

EXP-202 acceptance criteria:
- A create/update/delete appends exactly one event
- Replaying the stream reproduces record state
- Idempotent re-submit is a no-op

FAIL immediately if any check fails.
acceptance_criteria: Every MUST requirement acceptance criterion has a design element
No implementation code in the design artefact

result.summary: Design artefact src/design/entities.md validated — all 6 acceptance criteria for EXP-201 and EXP-202 are covered. Linter reports 0 BLOCKER, 3 MAJOR (E050: fenced code blocks > 40 lines). The 3 flagged blocks are: (1) ASCII data flow diagram, (2) entity definition JSON schema pseudocode, (3) public interface type signatures. All 3 are structural descriptions required by the validation checklist, not implementation code. No Zig function bodies, no SQL DDL in code blocks, no TypeScript. Migration schema uses Markdown tables (not code fences). Classification as Type E for both EXP-201 and EXP-202 is correct per lego-catalog selection rules.

issues.description: E050: 3 fenced code blocks exceed 40 lines (data flow diagram ~60 lines, JSON schema pseudocode ~60 lines, public interface signatures ~80 lines). All are structural descriptions, not implementation code. Acceptable for Type E design.
